chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said:
I heard al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'God did not send any Prophet at all except with the prohibition of wine and that he acknowledge to God [the doctrine of] al-Bada'.'

key_terms.بِالْبَدَاءِ: al-Bada' — the Shia theological doctrine that God may revise His decree according to His will, affirming divine omnipotence and freedom from any constraint of prior determination
key_terms.بِتَحْرِيمِ الْخَمْرِ: prohibition of wine/intoxicants — a universal law binding every prophet across all eras

ai.seo_question: What two universal obligations did God give every Prophet according to Imam al-Ridha in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) declares that every Prophet sent by God was commissioned with two universal obligations: the prohibition of intoxicants and affirmation of al-Bada' — the Shia theological doctrine affirming God's absolute freedom to revise His decrees. Reported by al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, a trusted companion of the Imam, this hadith pairs a concrete jurisprudential ruling with a core creedal belief, presenting both as inseparable from every prophetic mission throughout history.
